credentials.description: client_id of the environment (sandbox: developer account dashboard; production: Settings → API Keys, v4)

parameters.name: X-Trace-Id
parameters.description: A unique identifier to track this operation. It must be between 12 and 255 characters in length.

example_prompt: Fetch a Flutterwave virtual account to re-display its bank details and expiry to the customer.

amount.description: The amount to be collected. Specify `0` for static accounts.

reference.description: A custom identifier to track the transaction, This must be unique across all your transactions.

status.description: The status of the virtual account.

account_expiration_datetime.description: The expiry date and time of the virtual account.

note.description: A message providing instructions for the bank transfer, which includes the narration provided in the request.

created_datetime.description: The date and time when the virtual account was created..

customer_reference.description: This is the reference the customer sends as narration when making the bank transfer

narration.description: This allows you specify the name shown when the account is resolved.

message.description: Present on 401/403/409 bodies; the 400 body has none.

type.description: Error category. Generic: REQUEST_NOT_VALID, UNAUTHORIZED, FORBIDDEN, RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, RESOURCE_CONFLICT, UNPROCESSABLE, INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR; or a domain type (see code).

code.description: String. Generic 10400/10401/10403/10404/10409/10422/10500, or a domain code documented for this endpoint: 1900404 VIRTUAL_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND.

gotchas: Auth: one token server for both environments — the docs' Multi-Environment Integrations example sends either environment's credentials to https://idp.flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token, and Authentication says "This process applies to both the sandbox and production environments. Make sure to use the correct credentials for each environment to obtain a valid token." "Each token is valid for **10 minutes**"; "We recommend refreshing the token at least one minute before it expires." Cache the token. Sandbox: "We archive your test data after 30 days."

Headers: X-Trace-Id is optional on this GET (the headers guide lists it under 'Optional API Headers'; "It must be a string using only alphanumeric ASCII characters.", 12-255 characters). The API reference documents no X-Idempotency-Key for this endpoint.
Display data.account_number, data.account_bank_name and data.account_expiration_datetime. amount is 0 on static accounts; status is active or inactive.
This does not tell you whether the customer paid: payments arrive as charges (charge.completed webhook, list_charges?virtual_account_id=…).

Errors: {"status":"failed","error":{"type","code","message","validation_errors"}}; error.code is a string and 400s carry validation_errors[{field_name,message}]. Besides the generic codes (10400 REQUEST_NOT_VALID, 10401, 10403 FORBIDDEN, 10404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, 10409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT, 10422 UNPROCESSABLE, 10500) the error table documents these for this endpoint: 1900404 VIRTUAL_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND. Branch on error.type / error.code, not on the HTTP status alone. Docs (Errors): "The current limit is 500 API requests per minute." A 429 can come back as a non-JSON page ("HTML error pages such as `Cloudflare 1015 responses`"): parse error bodies defensively and back off exponentially with jitter.
open_questions: Token URL: the PHP sample of Authentication uses https://keycloak.dev-flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token; its curl and JavaScript samples and the Multi-Environment example use https://idp.flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token, which this spec follows.
